decisions.reason: The anamnesis app is the flagship product line, close to the core and central to the digital practice strategy, and a growing firm faces no aspiration shortfall that would prompt dropping it.
The education institute reuses existing training content, strengthens customer loyalty at modest cost, and the firm's slack lets it carry the product without a performance trigger for search.
Remote screen sharing has become standard support infrastructure since the pandemic, is cheap to run, and makes service more efficient, so there is no gap justifying its removal.
The analytics dashboard extends the core software into data-driven practice management, in line with the firm's direction, and slack allows it to mature even though its results remain uncertain.
The complete practice bundle mainly repackages core offerings for new practices, so it costs little and supports growth, though it could be restructured or renamed.

The job and practice portal is distant from core competencies and faces strong specialised competitors, making it the likeliest candidate for problemistic search, but its low cost and the community value it adds argue for keeping it for now.
